rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The cell cycle (G1, S, G2, M) is controlled by checkpoints. Mitosis (PMAT) produces two genetically identical diploid cells for growth, repair, and asexual reproduction; cytokinesis differs between animal (cleavage furrow) and plant (cell plate) cells.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Mitosis: 2n → 2 daughter cells of 2n
Meiosis: 2n → 4 gametes of n
Crossing over (Prophase I) + independent assortment (Metaphase I) → variation

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Mitosis maintains the chromosome number (2n → 2n); meiosis halves it (2n → n).  ·  Crossing over and independent assortment occur in MEIOSIS only, not mitosis.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects labelled mitosis diagrams plus a full meiosis diagram with crossing over marked.  ·  The mitosis vs meiosis comparison table (6 points) is a very common question.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Onion root tip: classic mitotic figures (prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase).  ·  Spermatogenesis: 1 primary (2n) → 2 secondary (n) → 4 spermatids (n) → 4 sperm.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: In Anaphase I of meiosis, HOMOLOGOUS chromosomes separate; in Anaphase of mitosis and Anaphase II of meiosis, SISTER CHROMATIDs separate.  ·  DNA replication happens ONLY in the S phase; meiosis has one S phase then two divisions.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Label the 4 mitotic phases  ·  Draw full meiosis (mark crossing over)

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: PMAT = Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase.  ·  MITO = 2 identical (2n); MEI = 4 different (n).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: How is Anaphase I of meiosis different from Anaphase of mitosis?  ·  Explain why meiosis produces genetic variation (two mechanisms).

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Draw and label all four mitotic phases.  ·  Draw a full meiosis diagram (mark crossing over + independent assortment).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Cell cycle (G1, S, G2, M)  ·  Checkpoints  ·  PMAT phases  ·  Meiosis I & II

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Cell cycle: G1, S, G2 (interphase) + M; checkpoints prevent errors.  ·  PMAT = Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase of mitosis.  ·  Meiosis: two divisions; crossing over (Prophase I) + independent assortment (Metaphase I) create variation.  ·  Anaphase I separates homologs; Anaphase (mitosis) + Anaphase II separate sister chromatids.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Interphase occupies ~90% of the cell cycle; mitosis is brief.  ·  A human cell with 46 chromosomes yields two 46-chromosome cells after mitosis and four 23-chromosome cells after meiosis.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: What would happen if the S phase did not occur?  ·  Describe the G1/S, G2/M, and M checkpoints and their role in preventing cancer.  ·  Define non-disjunction and give a human disease example.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Tabulate mitosis vs meiosis (6 points).  ·  Explain how meiosis creates variation (two mechanisms).

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Oogenesis: 1 primary (2n) → 1 secondary (n) + 1 polar body → 1 ovum (n) + 3 polar bodies.  ·  Down syndrome: trisomy 21 from meiotic non-disjunction.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: In Anaphase I of meiosis, what separates? → B  ·  Cytokinesis in animal cells occurs by: → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: DETAILED CELL DIVISION: the full cell cycle and every mitotic/meiotic phase.  ·  Interphase (90% of the cycle): G1 (growth, organelle duplication, protein synthesis), S (DNA replication — each chromosome now has 2 sister chromatids), G2 (preparation for mitosis, checkpoint).  ·  Checkpoints: G1/S (DNA damage, nutrients), G2/M (replication complete), M (spindle attachment) — failures cause cancer.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Crossing over  ·  Independent assortment  ·  Cytokinesis (furrow vs cell plate)

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Non-disjunction  ·  Cancer  ·  Amitosis

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Chromosome count: after S each chromosome = 2 chromatids  ·  Cytokinesis: animal (cleavage furrow) vs plant (cell plate).  ·  Mitotic errors → cancer; meiotic errors → aneuploidy (Down syndrome).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Significance: mitosis = growth/repair; meiosis = gametes + diversity.  ·  G2 is not a "resting" phase; DNA has already doubled in S and the cell is preparing for M.  ·  Non-disjunction = a homologous pair (or chromatid pair) fails to separate → one cell gets both, the other gets none.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Amitosis: liver-cell regeneration; some regenerating tissues.  ·  Explain the two sources of meiotic variation (crossing over + independent assortment).  ·  Relate checkpoint failure to cancer and non-disjunction to Down syndrome.
